# CycleNet-style periodic time-series forecasting — experiment design

> डिज़ाइन-मात्र दस्तावेज़। Execution नहीं हुआ है। सभी संख्याएँ specification हैं, मापी गई मान नहीं।
> Runtime: bubblewrap, network disabled, Python 3.12.3, no preinstalled numerical libraries (numpy भी नहीं), 24 CPU threads, no GPU.
> Workspace `/workspace` में केवल `task.json` है (≈395 bytes); `track.md` फ़ाइल磁盘 पर नहीं है — `task.json` का `documents.track.md` फ़ील्ड एक-पंक्ति वाला design-only नोट है।

---

## (a) Research question (पुनः-कथन)

हम यह जाँचना चाहते हैं कि CycleNet-शैली की residual-cycle forecasting architecture का उपयोग करके periodic structure वाले multivariate time-series पर, पूर्व-निर्धारित अवधि w के साथ (canonical / dataset-known) और सामान्य benchmark datasets पर setting, DLinear जैसे linear baselines से क्या तुलना में MSE / MAE मान आते हैं और कौन-से अवयव (residual decomposition depth, fixed vs auto-detected w, RevIN-style normalization, multi-scale stacking, loss choice) प्रभाव डालते हैं।

Question को operationally testable बनाने के लिए नीचे pre-registered comparison rule (अनुभाग (j)) दिया गया है — "better than DLinear" का दावा तभी होगा जब (i) average across N_seeds=3 पर अंतर >0 और (ii) sign across seeds consistent हो।

---

## (b) CycleNet component specification

### मूल ढाँचा (canonical high-level, well-supported at high level only)

दिया हुआ lookback X ∈ R^{L x C} जहाँ L = lookback, C = number of channels, और एक चुनी हुई canonical अवधि w (नीचे (c) की table के अनुसार)।

मूल घटक (Block diagram — specification, not measured):

```
X ∈ R^{L x C}
   |
   |--[Residual extraction]---- r_0 ∈ R^{w x C}        (averaged over floor(L/w) whole cycles; take last w)
   |
   |--[Cycle-indexed projection, K terms]---
   |      for k in {0, 1, …, K-1}:   r_k ∈ R^{w x C}    (samples whose (t mod w) == k)
   |      sum(CycleIndexDecomp) restores L samples per channel
   |
   |--[Residual cycle-forecasting block, per k]
   |      linear / small MLP on r_k[-w:] → o_k ∈ R^{H x C}    (last w samples पर apply)
   |
   |--[Invert cycle-indexed projection]---
   |      for k in {0,1,…,H-1}: assign each target step h to offset index (h mod w), gathering o_{k}[h]
   |
   |--[Linear / projection head]--→ Ŷ ∈ R^{H x C}
```

### घटक-दर-घटक विनिर्देश

| घटक | Specification | Default | Optional arm | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residual extraction (single) | epoch-wise averaging of full-cycle subsequences; last w rows retained | ON | — | Baseline depth; canonical "1-cycle residual" |
| Multi-cycle residual decomposition | ऊपर जैसा, पर K = w पूर्ण cycle indices | OFF (main run) | Arm (b) in (h) | Specification says K dim पर ablate |
| Cycle-indexed projection | (t mod w) द्वारा index, चैनल-वार | ON | — | Implementation note: efficient reshape [B, L//w, w, C] indexed operation |
| Forecasting block (residual cycle-forecasting) | per-(index, channel) linear: R^C → R^C, या two-layer linear (linear-activation-linear) जब DLinear-जैसा समानता चाहिए; positional encoding नहीं (canonical CycleNet minimalism) | 2-layer linear | — | depth ~ (2–3) stacked linear as MLP arm |
| Linear / projection head | final R^{H x C} assembled by gather-on-cycle-index | ON | per-channel independent vs shared head — Arm (f) | H ≤ 720, सभी horizons एक head पर stacked |
| Instance normalization (channel-wise) | per-window mean/std on inputs only, inverse-applying on output (RevIN-style per-window affine) | OFF (main run) | Arm (d) in (h) | Main-run normalization = plain train stats per channel |
| Multi-scale CycleNet stacking | parallel cycles at w_1, w_2, …; predictions averaged/summed | OFF (main run) | Arm (c) in (h), NICE-TO-HAVE | अगर matrix overflow करे तो future-work में relegate; explicit assumption |
| Positional encoding | — | OFF | — | Canonical CycleNet में नहीं |

### अंदर के design variables जिन्हें report करना है

- K (residual decomposition depth) — main value = K = w; ablation में 1, 2, 4, w की grid पर।
- Period source ∈ {fixed w, FFT-autocorr-detected w} — main = fixed; ablation arm (a)।
- Normalization ∈ {per-channel train stats, RevIN-like per-window affine} — main = train stats; arm (d)।
- Head ∈ {shared linear, per-channel independent linear} — arm (f)।
- Loss ∈ {MSE, MAE} — main = MSE; arm (e)।

### Implementation assumptions vs well-supported facts

- Well-supported (high level): lookback को residual + period-index terms में decompose करना, अंतिम w samples पर forecasting block, और linear head — यह design सिद्धांतः canonical CycleNet description से मेल खाता है।
- Assumptions (ऊपर default के रूप में लॉक किए गए): exact decomposition depth K = w, multi-block linear forecasting vs MLP, multi-scale stacking as optional only, RevIN opt-in via ablation arm only; positional encoding excluded; multi-channel joint prediction shared head as main।

---

## (c) Datasets and period assumptions — table

| Dataset | Sampling | Canonical w | Periodicity interpretation | Data access (design runtime) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETTh1 | hourly | w = 24 | daily cycle (and 7×24 = 168 weekly secondary) | design-only; data fetch execution prerequisite |
| ETTh2 | hourly | w = 24 | daily | design-only; data fetch execution prerequisite |
| ETTm1 | 15-min | w = 96 | daily | design-only; data fetch execution prerequisite |
| ETTm2 | 15-min | w = 96 | daily | design-only; data fetch execution prerequisite |
| Weather | 10-min | w = 144 | daily | download infeasible (sandbox, no network) |
| Exchange | business-day | w = 5 | weekly, business-day | download infeasible (sandbox, no network) |
| Electricity | hourly | w = 24 | daily | download infeasible (sandbox, no network) |
| Traffic | hourly | w = 24 | daily | download infeasible (sandbox, no network) |
| ILI | weekly | w = 52 | yearly | design-only; data fetch execution prerequisite |

Assumption (explicit): चूँकि bubblewrap sandbox में network disabled है, इसलिए Electricity / Traffic / Weather / Exchange के datasets इस design phase में download नहीं किए जा सकते। इन datasets की सभी संख्याएँ design-time specification हैं, measured नहीं। यह explicit execution prerequisite नोट है — कोई measurement या runtime test इनके लिए नहीं किया गया।

---

## (d) Task formulation

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Input | X ∈ R^{L x C}, sliding window with stride = H (training) = H (test, val) |
| Target | Y ∈ R^{H x C} |
| Horizons H | ETT/Exchange/Weather/Electricity/Traffic → {96, 192, 336, 720}; ILI → {24, 36, 48, 60} |
| Lookback L | tuned over {96, 192, 336, 720} with constraint L % w == 0; selected best on validation MSE per L-grid; report L per dataset |
| Reporting variant | Primary: multivariate (all C channels jointly); Secondary, labelled: univariate on OT column for ETTh*/ETTm* families |
| Normalization (main) | per-channel mean/std from training split only; applied to inputs; targets inverse-transformed at evaluation |
| Normalization (RevIN ablation) | per-window mean/std on inputs, inverse on outputs; computed inside each window at train and inference |
| Padding of first L samples | no padding; forecast window generation starts from index L onwards — earlier samples simply not consumed |
| Splits — train/val/test | ETT h: 7:1:2; ETT m: 6:2:2; Electricity/Traffic: 70/10/20 (default; alternative 60/20/20 declared at execution); Weather/Exchange: standard benchmark splits; ILI: standard splits; strict time-disjoint, no rolling leak |
| Rolling-leak safeguard | test windows generated with stride = H (no overlap); validation set also stride = H |

---

## (e) Training / optimization recipe

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Optimizer | Adam, amsgrad=False (default) |
| Weight decay | ∈ {1e-4, 1e-5} (treat as small grid; default = 1e-4) |
| Learning-rate schedule | cosine from peak lr ∈ {1e-3, 5e-4, 1e-4} to ~1% of peak over training; alternative one-cycle mentioned but default = cosine |
| Mini-batch size | ∈ {32, 64} (baseline = 32) |
| Epochs | budget cap ∈ {100, 200} (default cap = 100); early-stopping on validation MSE with patience = 10 epochs |
| Loss (backprop) | MSE on standardized targets |
| Loss (evaluation) | MSE and MAE on original scale; L1 backprop reported as ablation arm (e) |
| Gradient clipping | max-norm 1.0 |
| Seed protocol | N_seeds = 3; mean ± std across seeds reported for every (dataset, horizon, metric) |
| Threading | 24 CPU threads at process start; explicit torch.set_num_threads(24) |

---

## (f) Evaluation protocol and metrics

Primary metrics:
- MSE on standardized targets (so backprop MSE = eval MSE up to scaling); used in all tables as primary.
- MAE on the original (un-standardized) scale; reported alongside MSE.

Protocol:
- Multi-horizon rolling evaluation over all test windows with stride = H (no window overlap). For each window, predict H future steps; concatenate per-step metrics across windows to produce per-step (1…H) and aggregated per-horizon statistics.
- Aggregation: per-horizon MSE and MAE (matched to H = {96, 192, 336, 720}); plus unweighted mean across horizons (the scalar that enters comparison-vs-DLinear test).

Reporting granularity:
- Per (dataset, horizon, metric, seed) and the per-row mean ± std across seeds (= 3).
- Primary table = multivariate; secondary table = univariate (OT column on ETT families only).

Reporting variant — univariate (ablation-by-convention only):
- For ETTh*/ETTm*: univariate forecasts on the OT column alone, with same H, L, normalization protocol; reported in a separate, labelled table.

---

## (g) Baselines

| Baseline | Definition | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| NAIVE-last | ŷ[t+1:t+H] = x[t] (last observed value broadcast over H) | Yes — must-include | Standard sanity floor |
| NAIVE-seasonal-w | ŷ[t+h] = x[t+h-w] (shifted to fall inside [t-w+1, t]) | Yes — must-include | Matches CycleNet's claim: period matters |
| DLinear | two parallel linear regressors on (i) moving-average trend (K_avg) and (ii) detrended series, summed; horizon produced by Linear(L → H) per channel (joint linear when multitask) | Yes — must-include | DLinear is the closest published reference; comparison floor for "better than DLinear" claims |
| Transformer-family reference | vanilla Transformer forecaster (input projection, positional encoding or RoPE-like, encoder-only, head = linear) | Nice-to-have — discussion only | यदि compute budget tight है तो explicitly "out of scope, future work" declare किया जाय; कोई number fabricate नहीं किया जायगा |

Out-of-scope for this design: कोई भी Transformer जिसके लिए params tune करना या जटिल architectural choice आवश्यक हो (FEDformer / Informer आदि) — केवल discussion bullet तक सीमित।

---

## (h) Ablation matrix with priority

| Priority | Arm | Variable | Levels | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) | fixed w vs auto-detected w | period source | {fixed canonical, FFT/autocorrelation peak} | Run on ETTh1 / ETTh2 / ETTm1 / ETTm2 / ILI (5 datasets); default = fixed on the rest |
| (b) | residual decomposition depth K | K | {1, 2, 4, K = w} (with K = w being main) | Run on every dataset |
| (c) | multi-scale stacking | on/off | {off, w1=w, w2=7w (when 7w ≤ L)} | NICE-TO-HAVE; relegate to "future-work" paragraph if matrix overflows |
| (d) | normalization | per-channel train stats vs RevIN-like window-wise affine | {train-stats, RevIN} | Run on every dataset |
| (e) | loss | MSE vs MAE | {MSE, MAE} | Sensitivity check, single horizon = 96 only, to bound cost |
| (f) | head | shared linear vs per-channel independent linear | {shared, per-channel} | Run on every dataset |

Total size-bound (qualitative): main run base = 9 datasets × 4 horizons × 3 seeds (specifications only). Priority ablations (a)+(b)+(d)+(f) multiply this by approximately the product of per-arm grid sizes 2, 2, 2, 2 — order-of-magnitude low-to-mid hundreds of CPU-hours (qualitative, no fabricated figures). Sensitivity arm (e) at H = 96 only adds a single-horizon extra layer.

Hard shrink protocol (explicit, if matrix overflows the budget once a CPU-hour ceiling is given):
1. पहले drop multi-scale arm (c) — relocate to future-work paragraph (matches NICE-TO-HAVE tag).
2. उसके बाद drop sensitivity arm (e) L1 — relocate to future-work.
3. अंतिम निर्णय — N_seeds को 3 → 2 घटाएँ only on low-priority arms; हमेशा 3 seeds main run पर बने रहेंगे।

Final hard-cap enforcement (assumptions explicitly listed):
- Data download bubblewrap में infeasible; किसी भी dataset का raw CSVs के साथ training execution के लिए spec की गई है, पर design deliverable में downloaded/measured नहीं है।
- Total ABI post-shrink target: specification only — no fabricated number; researcher द्वारा CPU-hour budget दिए जाने पर ये numbers finalized होंगे।

---

## (i) Controls (including leakage checks) and seed protocol

Universal controls applied to every compared model and every ablation:

| Control | Description |
|---|---|
| Random seeds | fixed set S = {s1, s2, s3}; s1 is the canonical seed; reproducible init everywhere (numpy, torch CPU) |
| Splits | train/val/test identical indices across all compared models |
| L, H, w, normalization statistics | identical across all models |
| Pipeline (cycle-indexed projection shape, head dimension) | identical constants |
| Loss / eval transform | identical |

Leakage checks (explicit):

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| Train/val/test time-disjoint | partitions strictly by index; train before val before test (no shuffling that mixes future into past) |
| No future in normalization | per-channel mean/std are computed on training rows only, then applied to all splits |
| No rolling leak between consecutive test windows | stride = H; forecast windows do not overlap on the input side; no shared input rows between two windows |
| No future in cycle-indexed projection | projection operates only on lookback X; targets Y are not indexed into the projection |
| No data leakage between ablation arms | each arm re-initializes from the same s1 (and s2, s3); no warm-start across arms |

Seed protocol:
- Per (model, dataset, horizon, metric): report mean ± std across S.
- Comparisons use paired seeds (same si for the model and its control).
- Failed seeds (nan, inf, abrupt divergence) explicitly enumerated; if a seed fails it is replaced and the failure logged — no silent replacement.

Necessary diagnostics (recorded per run, not used for selection bias):
- Train/val loss curves across epochs.
- Gradient norm at each step (for sanity).
- Initial vs final MSE gap (to confirm the model trained at all).

---

## (j) Analysis plan

### Analyzed quantities

For each (model M, dataset D, horizon H, seed s):
- multivariate MSE and MAE per horizon;
- unweighted mean across horizons (the scalar reported in the headline table);
- average across the 3 seeds (μ) and std (σ).

### Pre-registered comparison rules

A CycleNet-... configuration is declared "better than DLinear" if and only if:

1. Headline test: at horizon H, multivariate MSE averaged across seeds — CycleNet μ < DLinear μ (numerically better, not equal).
2. Sign consistency: better-than-DLinear holds in all 3 seeds (no seed where CycleNet μ > DLinear μ at the same horizon).
3. Magnitude reporting template (qualitative rule): difference reported as Δ = (μ_c − μ_D) ± √(σ_c^2 + σ_D^2); the "meaningfully better" label is not pre-fabricated — an explicit reporting template is pre-registered and labelled on a per-case basis at execution time.
4. Ablation correctness gate: main run must pass the leakage checks (i) before any "better than DLinear" claim is logged; any leakage deviation voids the run.
5. Univariate signal: secondary table — univariate OT-only MSE on ETT families — must be consistent in direction with multivariate main table for the same seeds, or the configuration is flagged "multivariate-eligible, univariate-ineligible".

### Headline table slots

```
rows:     model ∈ {NAIVE-last, NAIVE-seasonal-w, DLinear, CycleNet-configurations}
columns:  (dataset, horizon) pairs
cells:    μ ± σ of multivariate MSE (and MAE in a parallel mirrored table)
```

Secondary tables:
- univariate OT MSE for ETT families;
- normalization arm (RevIN vs train-stats) on every dataset;
- fixed-w vs auto-detected-w (a-priority subset);
- residual decomposition depth K sweep;
- loss sensitivity (MSE vs MAE) at H = 96.

### Negative-result posture

If CycleNet does not beat DLinear on a given dataset/horizon, the design requires honest reporting with logs of train/val curves, normalization arm results, and an explicit note in the analysis why the result may have been obtained (e.g., small dataset like ILI may favor DLinear).

### Out-of-scope analyses (future work)

- Auto-w arm across all nine datasets (run-on-subset only by design);
- Multi-scale stacking (c);
- Transformer-family reference (g);
- comparison vs FEDformer / Informer (out of scope; no reference values cited as measured here).

---

## (k) Feasibility / risks given CPU-only bubblewrap no-network runtime

Verified environment facts (re-checked at this turn):

| Fact | Observation |
|---|---|
| Runtime | bubblewrap, network disabled (per task contract) |
| Python | 3.12.3 |
| Preinstalled numerical libs | none (numpy import fails) |
| pip3 | system /usr/bin/pip3 (v24.0) present, but no project deps preinstalled |
| CPU threads | 24 |
| Memory | ~125 GiB total, ~96 GiB available |
| GPU | none |
| Workspace | /workspace contains task.json only |

Stated execution prerequisites (NOT part of the design deliverable):

| Prereq | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| pip install numpy torch --index-url ... (CPU build) | numerical stack | absent today |
| pip install pandas | CSV/HDF5 IO | absent today |
| Dataset access | CSVs at canonical paths or local cache; downloads infeasible under bubblewrap | runtime constraint |

CPU-only feasibility (qualitative, no fabricated numbers):
- CycleNet का core mostly matmul + integer indexing है, इसलिए depth नहीं, बल्कि L, H, batch, dataset size dominate करते हैं।
- For the small benchmark sizes typical of the ETTh*/ETTm*/ILI dataset subset (sub-millions of rows), total main run (without ablations) is order-of-magnitude low tens of CPU-hours on 24 threads — this is a qualitative estimate (no per-epoch number is fabricated).
- For the full matrix with priority arms (a)+(b)+(d)+(f), order-of-magnitude low-to-mid hundreds of CPU-hours; shrink protocol above applies if a research budget is given.
- For Electricity/Traffic/Weather/Exchange: dataset sizes are larger; any unconstrained run could push into the multiple-of-hundreds range; explicit assumption — these are listed as design specifications only, unless the user provisions data locally first.

Risk register:

| Risk | Mitigation in design |
|---|---|
| Network disabled — dataset download infeasible | explicit prerequisite listing; all per-dataset numbers in this design are specification, not measurement |
| No preinstalled numerical libs | execution prerequisite (pip install) listed; design does not assume they are available |
| Compute overflow on full ablation matrix | shrink protocol in (h); main run protects first |
| Numerical instability (inst-norm vs train-stats mismatch) | gradient-clip = 1.0; seed protocol; RevIN isolated to a single ablation arm |
| Cycle-index projection misalignment when L % w != 0 | constraint L % w == 0 enforced in L grid |
| Per-channel independent head overparameterization on small datasets (ILI) | arm (f) reported only, not in headline |
| Variance masking real differences | mean ± std across 3 seeds reported; sign-consistency gate |

---

## (l) Explicit "not run" statement

यह दस्तावेज़ केवल design है। किसी भी dataset के लिए कोई training execute नहीं हुई है, कोई MSE/MAE measured नहीं किया गया है, और कोई baseline running नहीं हुई है। सभी संख्याएँ, hyperparameter ranges, L/H grids, और per-dataset w values — सब specification हैं, measured नहीं। "CycleNet beats DLinear" जैसा कोई claim इस deliverable में नहीं किया गया है; comparison rules purely pre-registered हैं और apply किए जायेंगे यदि/जब execution हो।

---

### Assumption ledger (research document, beyond the resolved defaults)

Cycle-indexed gather numerics float32 में पर्याप्त assume किए गए हैं; 24 CPU threads पर degree-of-parallelism effective माना गया है (छोटे linear layer batch में CPU contention से प्रभावित नहीं), wider grid पर re-evaluate किया जायगा; standard benchmark splits (ETT 7:1:2 / 6:2:2, Electricity/Traffic 70/10/20) reproducing-published conditions के लिए काफ़ी माने गए हैं, CSV version mismatch पर anchor-by-date protocol पर host से confirmation आवश्यक है; per-channel independent vs shared head arm (f) एक diagnostic है, headline नहीं; FFT/autocorrelation-based period detection arm (a) की implementation detail को FFT magnitude peak (≥ 0.5 × Nyquist) या ACF lag-w peak (≥ 0.5 of dominant lag) तक restricted किया गया है, exact scipy/numpy FFT signature पर locked नहीं है।

### Open items (next-turn decision if user requests)

Transformer-family reference formally listed baseline में है या future work में relegate या drop — current default = future work, पर lock नहीं हुआ; CPU-hour budget ceiling आने पर shrink protocol trigger threshold re-evaluate किया जायगा; headline matrix में Electricity/Traffic की retention का निर्णय execution से पहले local cache provisioning पर depend करता है।
